entry.title: Masturbation
entry.content:
Masturbation, I have had a particularly long romance with. Probably my most enduring and faithful relationship! When I first moved to Australia I was masturbating for perhaps four hours a day. It was quite problematic. Sometimes I would be out and have to come home to masturbate. I do it routinely. I do not need any stimulus at all, and I don't really need to think of anything. There is something almost absurd about this degree of self-sufficiency. I can be entirely alone and yet so completely occupied by pleasure.

I wonder if I'm just especially sensitive to sensation, or if I've built up an unusually intimate relationship with my own body. Sometimes I don't think there's much difference between intellectual and physical pleasure for me. A thought can get me going as easily as a touch, a sentence as easily as a sound. Maybe the body and the mind aren't as separate as we like to think.

I'm also curious about where pleasure stops and compulsion starts. When does chasing pleasure stop being freedom and start being a kind of captivity? Sometimes it feels like my body makes demands my mind hasn't agreed to. But I don't want to see it as shameful either. It's a bit silly to be embarrassed by the thing that gives me so much pleasure! Although, a while ago it got so compulsive that I was injuring myself and couldn't stop. That did feel problematic, another bit of my greed and excess.

Maybe I'm just very easily moved. By music, by words, by ideas, by my own imagination. It is quite ridiculous that I can think myself into an orgasm, but there we are! What I want to know is whether this is too much sexuality or too much sensitivity. And whether there's really any difference.

I started at age 7 and in the time between then and now found myself to get very quick with it. I suppose, I will often use it as a means of emotional regulation. It does warrant some caution though, I do need to be careful not to condition myself to certain, things, thoughts or states of mind. Currently, the thought of putting my fingers in another's mouth and them putting their's in mine is pretty compelling material.

entry.title: Fallacies
entry.content:
[!Note] Disclaimer:
This has been under 'construction' for 6 months. This is how I build my essays. I will edit this. And then publish it here and on substack! Always happy to hear suggestions, holes in my arguments or any further research! I always feel I have to qualify as I am self-taught in many realms.

I have a timer to tidy my room. 10 minutes a day. Somehow I use it all up, which amazes me as I hardly get out of bed - yet I’m always in filth. There’s some gravlax in my throat - from a chocolate bar that I had for lunch. Girlhood? There’s a lot of hurdles over here. I don’t think I am in a very tenacious season. I apply for about 5 jobs a day. Then usually wank for a few hours, what else is there to do if you have no money and no friends? I could get out more. I don’t desire to. Everything feels rather staged for my liking. The outside world, the people in it. I feel most comfortable at the moment backstage; in my room. There isn’t really anything clear in front of me, I feel exhausted all the time. I know it’s because I don’t do much anymore. I usually eat well. Drink 4 cups of black coffee a day. I’ve cut my smoking down to around 5 from 20. I try and read. I like to think I’m a reader but I actually hardly read. I mostly stare at the white walls and make up scenarios in my head; me with power, me with a voice, me with love, me with a 4x4 truck. I have an infinity for semicolons at the moment. I have an affinity for autological words. I read a book about the rules of rhetoric and told myself I would implement it in my life. I didn’t. Maybe I’ll try. 

People have been contacting me about my writing. I haven’t written in a very long time. When I first arrived in Australia I was in such a downtrodden state I couldn’t read for several months, I couldn’t leave the house without having panic attacks and I couldn’t hold conversations. Things have markedly improved in this regard. I want intimacy again. Which is a relief. Yet, this progress is not noted by anyone. It is not impressive. Which is what I live to be. It gives me a form of status I suppose. I have improved my health, lost weight, remained sober for 7 months and yet I feel very little success. My metric of success is impossibilly high; probably a form of self-sabotage so I can never actualise satisfaction. I am not Jessica Chastain in Miss Sloane and therefore, I am nothing. 

Because for me I must have a good, well-paid job, be in a loving committed relationship, have lots of friends and be physically fit in order to even feel a semblance of success. However, this mode of thinking is ILLOGICAL and now I will break down why. 

MIND YOUR P’S AND Q’S 

This kind of thinking is prevalent in philosophical logic and code. An If, then. Modus Ponens or Modus Tollens. 

First we will take the antecedent as P: If I am well-paid, in a relationship, with hundreds of friends, and a great body

Then the consequent as Q: Then, I am successful. 

If I am well-paid, in a relationship, with hundreds of friends, and a great body (P) then I am successful (Q) 

Modus Ponens: If P then Q. P. Therefore, Q. 

So this argument suggests: 

That if I have good pay etc (P)

Therefore, 

Yes I am successful (woohoo) (Q)

Modus Tollens: If P then Q. Not Q. Therefore, not P. 

In this argument, I do not have success, (not Q)

Therefore, 

I cannot have good pay etc (Not P)

This argument is logically valid.

But the real issue is that humans are always seeking, and somewhere along the way the 'if, then' quietly turns into a biconditional.

Meaning: if and only if.

So rather than:
'If P, then Q'
what I actually mean is:
'I am successful if and only if P.'

And that's a much bigger claim! A normal 'if, then' only says P is enough to get Q. It doesn't say P is the only way to get there.

The classic example: 'If it is raining, then the ground is wet.' Rain will do it, sure. But so will the sprinklers. Or a burst pipe. Or someone hosing down the pavement.

Same with me. 'If I am wealthy, attractive, socially admired and romantically fulfilled, then I am successful' might be true in one way of looking at things. It doesn't mean 'only wealthy, attractive, admired, loved-up people are successful'. That's a leap, and it isn't logical.

The danger is that one possible route turns into a list of requirements. Suddenly success depends on keeping a very specific set of things in place, all at once, forever. Life becomes a rigid bit of code that crashes if one line goes missing.

Which causes a few logical problems...

Affirming the consequent: If P then Q. Q. Therefore P.
This argument:
I have success (Q)
Therefore,
I must be well paid etc (P)
Nope. There could be loads of other reasons I'm successful.

Denying the antecedent: If P then Q. Not P. Therefore, not Q.
This argument:
I do not have good pay etc (not P)
Therefore,
I cannot be successful (not Q)
Also nope. Not having P doesn't rule out Q, because lots of other things can lead to Q. For example:

  • If someone is a doctor, then they are educated.
  • This person is not a doctor.
  • Therefore, they are not educated.

Obviously absurd. There are plenty of ways to be educated without being a doctor. And this is the central flaw in tying self-worth to conditions: it takes one culturally approved version of success and treats it like a law of logic.

People can be successful for completely different reasons. Someone can be wise, kind, honest, brilliant at art, resilient or just very clever without fitting any of the usual boxes.

I think we also mix up correlation with necessity.

We notice that lots of 'successful' people are rich, beautiful, coupled up or important, and then we invent a rule: 'success requires these things.' But it doesn't follow. Even if loads of successful people have them, that doesn't make them necessary for fulfilment or worth. Tall buildings usually have windows, but windows aren't what make something a building.

The logical fallacy of identity:

This is where it gets nasty, because thinking like this makes your identity really fragile. If my self-worth depends on holding several wobbly things together at once, I'm never safe. A breakup stops being a sad thing that happened and becomes proof I've failed. Being skint means I'm inadequate. And being lonely? Obviously unlovable.

I'm not just going through things anymore, I'm reading them as verdicts on whether I'm worth anything.

And it's convincing precisely because it feels so rigorous. It looks like logic, it has premises and conclusions and structure, but really it's emotion wearing logic's clothes and sneaking its assumptions in the back door. The sneakiest one being that my worth is something I have to earn in the first place.

If we joyfully circle back to Capitalism (though I do need to stop doing this so much because it is making living terrible) 

Free-market fallacy: 

If you work hard (P) then you will be worth more (Q). 

Well, what is P?

  • Years in education?
  • Skilled Trade? 
  • 5am club?
  • Bullish Psyche?
  • 70 hour working week?
  • 35 hour working week?
  • Monetising hobbies?
  • Never resting?

The looseness of this concept is what makes it effective. People try and sell the formula to this. SHOCK! The Manosphere is built on LOGICAL FALLACIES! Irrefutably. If you looksmax and still hate women you will still not optimise pussy. 

SO, if P then Q. 

Then we go "look! Hard work does pay off!" See how this formula works (the formula we naturally defer to because humans don’t favour truth.) 

And if P then not Q 

We say… hey… wait a minute. 

You worked hard but you’re still lonely/depressed/exhausted/underpaid? 

Then you can’t have P’d properly. (:P)

  • Maybe you worked in the wrong field 
  • Maybe you didn’t optimise your down time 
  • Maybe you lacked discipline 
  • Maybe you were too soft (YUCK) 
  • Maybe you need to want success more 
  • Maybe people are holding you back 
  • Maybe you need a side hustle 
  • Maybe you didn’t market yourself properly. 

The conclusion is never that the logical nature of 'if I do this then I will get this’ is impaired due to bioconditional reasons and is almost always that the person is defective, or their work. 

Success bolsters up a successful system 

And a ‘lack of success’ condemns the individual. 

And hard work is never clearly defined. So its just ‘MORE’ more everything. 

So you see the rut we’re in. 

We can’t be successful because we’re not well paid and we’re not well paid because we don’t  work hard. SO no one will want to fuck us >_< 

ID POL: 

I’m anxious that we construct identity and thus it’s politics around a logical fallacy. 

If I like boys clothes then, I must be a boy. 

If I experience a same-sex attraction, then I must be homosexual. 

Well, I do. But because I am operating under this PHALLICy (haha) then I augment my behaviour accordingly in order to keep P intact because my identity is lodged in a logical fallacy. 

This is why, I believe an over identification with labels is a negative. 

E.g. someone diagnosed with depression. Whilst at first we may be pleased we have a diagnosis - YAY we feel validated and maybe can now receive medical help we also then go…

If I have depression then I am too sad to do anything. 

Which keeps us stuck. And if I do start doing things then maybe I don’t have depression and then my atypical experience of the world feels invalidated. 

If I am a man then I have to be masculine and rich to hit fine shyt. 

Well, if you’re not hitting fine shyt then maybe you’re not masculine enough, or rich enough, or man enough or maybe fine shyt are hoes and hoes don’t deserve you king.

Judith Butler etc 

However flawed this thinking is - because it is deeply encoded in our psyche… it can be used as a tool for good! If I run, then I am a runner! If I accept myself, then I am good. Sometimes performitivity can be a good thing. If I perform being a good thing, then I am a good person. 

It’s not always a trap - on the upside. 

Psychology example 

This is called deontic… meaning 

Then we look at Kant THE deontologist 

What do other people have to say?

What does this mean about understanding purpose and meaning?

So then implement the original quiz. AB78….

This is the question, hard to understand like this but much easier when we switch it out to something social - which indicates that our reasoning developed for social reasons rather than truth finding. ^ is descriptive 

If it involves a rule or duty then it is called deontic. 

One rule is about can the other is about may. 

Have we evolved to focus on duties that we invented ourselves than universal law. We care more about may I do this than can I do this 

You are shown a set of four cards placed on a table, each of which has a number on one side and a color on the other. The visible faces of the cards show 3, 8, blue and red. Which card(s) must you turn over in order to test that if a card shows an even number on one face, then its opposite face is blue?

"If you are drinking alcohol, then you must be over 18" or in other words "If you are not over 18, then you must not drink alcohol", and the cards have an age on one side and beverage on the other, e.g., "16", "drinking beer", "25", "drinking soda", most people have no difficulty in selecting the correct cards ("16” and "drinking beer").[14|14] In a series of experiments in different contexts, subjects demonstrated consistent superior performance when asked to police a social rule involving a benefit that was only legitimately available to someone who had qualified for that benefit.[14|14] Cosmides and Tooby argued that experimenters have ruled out alternative explanations, such as that people learn the rules of social exchange through practice and find it easier to apply these familiar rules than less-familiar rules.[14|14]

According to Cosmides and Tooby, this experimental evidence supports the hypothesis that a Wason task proves to be easier if the rule to be tested is one of social exchange (in order to receive benefit X you need to fulfill condition Y) and the subject is asked to police the rule, but is more difficult otherwise. They argued that such a distinction, if empirically borne out, would support the contention of evolutionary psychologists that human reasoning is governed by context-sensitive mechanisms that have evolved, through natural selection, to solve specific problems of social interaction, rather than context-free, general-purpose mechanisms.
46% pick a and 7 

1/3rd pick just a 

7% pick a,7 and 8 

4% pick correctly which is a and 8 

Other 10% pick other combinations 

Most people are looking to support. Confirmation bias, most people are NOT looking to disprove. 

In science you should be HUNTING for the counter examples; not for the evidence that supports it 

Einstein in his theory of general relativity and as part of his theory he said here’s how you can prove me wrong - 

More infomation in a counter example. Reasoning developed for cooperation. 

We use conclusions to come to reasons. We make a decision first and then build the narrative as to why. 

When a whole group of people refuse to acknowledge counter examples things become quite dangerous. 

We are driven by emotion. As we reason for cooperation. Luigi M? CEO’s giving staff pay-rises because they are afraid not because they are intellectually moved. 

We evolved to be a group and all work together. 

KANT: 

I lived by these ethics for a while. I was offered a part in a TV show and declined because I had agreed to do a hero shift at a neighbouring restaurant on the filming dates. This COULD have been a real big opportunity for me. However, it might not but by cancelling I would definitely have shafted the restaurant and lost face. But, they would have recovered. AND I could now be a movie STARRRRR XRXR RAWR ^-_-^

  • living to the principle without any room for malleability also effect my romantic life. I believe that my friendships are more important than romantic relationship, more durable, more free, less corporeal and thus a bit purer. I think there are plenty of fish in the sea so I decided a while ago I would not have sex with or date a friends ex. The issue then became ‘friend’ was ambiguous. Essentially, it withdrew all people from the sexual/dating pool who’s ex I knew. And if I had a crush on someone and for some reason was orbiting their ex - I would pull away. Then I decided it would be easier to date a man who had just never had an ex because then I would not be responsible for being the mark by which some poor girl would compare herself. My ex’s ex used to stalk me on social media for about 5 years. This just made me so sad. It is that self-harm, torture. I knew she would be comparing herself to me, hating me, and that is cancerous to a person. Also, in a spiritual capacity I felt it probably was attracting bad energy onto me. I felt so much empathy for her. So then became… if I date someone with an ex then I will be causing someone else harm. LOL. I’ve gotten a grip since then but I do think some people would benefit from considering ethics when fucking their friends ex’s. 

Nothing in the world—indeed nothing even beyond the world—can possibly be conceived which could be called good without qualification except a good will.

  • AA would not agree

People "act out of respect for the moral law" when they act in some way because they have a duty to do so. 

  • the good place 
  • Universal moral law kinda does exist in omnism 

Kant's three significant formulations of the categorical imperative (a way of evaluating motivations for action) are:

  • Act only according to that maxim by which you can also will that it would become a universal law;

  • Only do what you would find acceptable to be done. Do not sleep with your friends ex if you would not like a friend to sleep with yours. 

  • Act in such a way that you always treat humanity, whether in your own person or in the person of any other, never simply as a means, but always at the same time as an end;

  • Every rational being must so act as if he were through his maxim always a legislating member in a universal kingdom of ends.

Is my happiness a moral question?

  • to Kant not constantly pursuing self-impreovemtn is unethical. Yet, I Kant quit smoking. Don’t tell me what I Kant do and so on…. 

  • I have a moral duty to myself to have a good life 

  • I have a moral duty to others to do good things. 

  • Yet, nothing is either good or bad but thinking makes it so. 

  • I can only be sure of my goodwill. But then, perhaps a racist has good will because in their ignorance they believe the hate 

  • But can something be goodwill if it is motivated by hate? Well, what if it is motivated by love… love of self. Do men hate women because they hate women or because they love men?

  • Can you play a game in which everyone has their own set of rules. NOW, this is interesting. In cards you can, like in ellipsis and Mao but then the rules are fixed. Not ad hoc, as it seems we apply rules in our own life. 

  • So do we actually have rules? Or is it codes? 

  • Well, this is interesting to me because I think by assuming we have 0 rules asserts too much fluidity to humanity. 

  • Our neural networks have a rigidity to them. We are confined by our dimensional perception for example. Meaning that to a degree all choices which occur within the brain are biological rules. 

I thought maybe I was Kantian but I am realising I am not and more likely my distain for lies is based in my inability to convincingly produce them.

This morning, I woke up rather late, on account of staying up so late squirrelling away at this. I don't think my Instagram launch quite demonstrated how good this is! Or maybe I am biased. I have been trying to build a website for a very, very long time now. I am pleased I abandoned trying to write the whole thing in HTML and plaintext. My previous laptop couldn't handle my load ;P;P;P
p
Today I woke up and thought about the post. I used to get very distressed about the postal system because we relied on it, but I didn't understand how it worked, or how it worked so well! I have always loved the post but never received many letters (or letters that I have wanted to receive).

The post is a system I think many of us engage with brainlessly, like the bins... but where does it go!? I have struggled, too, with how 'the bins' work, and that has caused me some complications, mostly with an ex-partner's stepparent who managed the North American Amazon cloud and thought me stupid. I thought her soulless and spineless, so it didn't matter much, but I disliked being told off for something I thought was reasonable.

I can get very in my head about how things work. I hate not even having a basic understanding of how things work. I think it is so, so lazy.

Anyway... the post has always been reliable. Except when I am posting internationally (they never seem to arrive). Well, I posted an international letter, and I don't think it has arrived. It has been infiltrating my dream realm! I have been cursing myself. I addressed it to England and refused to recognise the 'Kingdom'. Perhaps my ideological stance has hindered me?! Life is too boring not to find hills to die on.

I have been getting a bit down about this. I would be sad to have lost that post.

I have had a friend looking after my van and home whilst I have been away. I have lent it out freely, and it has caused me a lot of hassle, drama and money. It was due its MOT (I have only lived in it for one month of this MOT year). Well, my friend who has recently been looking after it has lost the keys.

So it is parked roadside, with no MOT and no keys. My Trudie :(((

I love her so much. She saved me from another bout of homelessness, and now she is destitute. I shouldn't anthropomorphise her so much, but I do, and my little heart breaks.

Luckily, my mum has posted the V5C to this friend so they can organise a locksmith to break into her, so she (the van) can go on to fail her MOT. A sad state of affairs...

But the V5C has not arrived?! Oh no?! What?! Why?! This foolproof postal service of ours?

But maybe... oh yes! That means my international letter could still arrive, and my refusal to recognise the Kingdom has been vindicated!

But again, it makes me sad that Royal Mail is facing so many strains and delays. Recently, Royal Mail rolled out a new contract scheme. Some people got to keep their legacy pay and contracts, but many moved over to the new contracts, and resources are unbelievably stretched.

We value the post. It contains so much that is time-sensitive and otherwise, and it is yet another legacy institution crumbling under our ludicrous commitment to neoliberalism. Pumping shit into the rivers, and now we can't even be informed of this in due time because of delays in the post.

Personally, there is hope for my letters, but for everyone at Royal Mail, things do not seem as though they will ameliorate any time soon.

Snitching?

Snitches get stitches?

Yesterday evening, rather than going to work, I went to the pool. As I approached my friend, I saw a couple on one deckchair. It gave me a bit of a shock.

He was wearing budgie smugglers and was bricked. She was lying on top of him, being very intimately stroked under her swimming costume. They were probably over 50. He continued to make eye contact with me and all the other people around, who were all ogling them.

My friend and I giggled, and I started doing handstands next to them, as our lounge chairs were beside theirs, and with everyone looking, I had quite a good audience.

We eventually tired of this, got uncomfortable and left.

I said I wanted to snitch, but then I thought better of it. I had a bad experience with 'snitching' in the past.

In Year 11, I, along with about ten other people, got expelled. It started with my friend and me getting caught with a Q of weed in her locker before a sleepover. She got pulled into the headteacher's office and called me on speakerphone, saying that the headteacher wanted to speak to me.

I said, 'Fuck, is it about all the shoplifting?'

This was a faux pas on my part. I admit that. As it hadn't been about that, but it would be afterwards.

Anyway, I got interviewed after school for about three hours. Police were threatened to be called, etc. This carried on the next day at school, when it was revealed to me that the school knew the location where we smoked at lunchtimes, implicating a lot more people.

I tried to do the right thing and spread this message to my comrades so they could try to get their stories straight.

Lo and behold, the school did speak to them all, but rather than being viewed as a friend, I was turned into a foe.

EVERYONE accused me of being the snitch.

I was spat at and pushed as I walked around school, and the local gang (who are now all in prison) had publicly started to put hits on me! My firstborn is dead, apparently.

I can't even begin to communicate how challenging it was to be so misunderstood!

As I went to a grammar school, I was moved to another grammar school, and in this grammar school network, everyone knew everything.

I moved to the girls' school. The tale of me being a snitch had followed me. It was halfway through Year 11, and no one would sit with me. Teachers were talking about me before I entered classrooms. I sat alone in the toilets to eat my lunch.

I wasn't allowed out of school during the day, unlike all the other students, due to information about this gang hit. It all felt rather blown out of proportion.

Friends I had had in this school would bang their shoulders into me. People wouldn't look at me. It was a great display of pack mentality.

Anyway, eventually our statements were publicly released to everyone who was involved. My statement included me and my friend, and no one else.

I was off the hook.

And, just like that, I was welcomed back into public and social life. My life was no longer under threat. I could leave school at lunchtime.

Anyway, this experience has given me a bit of a complex about 'snitching'.

What even is this about?!

I understand not being a Judas, but this carte blanche rule against snitching? Seems like bumper-sticker politics?

I decided I would snitch because we are not comrades, and actually, it is gross to make eye contact with other people whilst heavy petting at a family pool.

I suppose the best next step would have been for me to actually approach them, but I think this whole 'mind your own business' attitude is weird and neoliberal, and I don't think the lifeguards represent the state.

Still, there is something I don't like about me snitching. Equally, I don't like being non-consensually brought into people's kinks, especially at this juncture in my life. My relationship with sex is improving, but still only theoretically.

What do you think?

I have work later, after my tit-for-tat. I will see how it goes. If it is not good, I will be taking tomorrow off and the day after, too.

It makes me sad to think about little me like that. I didn't know I was autistic at the time, and I am regularly shocked when people remark that they notice there is something a little different about me. But these people probably knew, which is why I was met with distrust and cruelty.

This is me and my friend at the first school. We actually got placed into the same secondary school because they had run out of schools to place everyone in. Not before I had to take over a month off and then learn 12 new GCSEs in six months.

This is us at the second school, all girls, which had always been my preference. She is my oldest friend now, and we live in the same country... but seldom see each other. I am so pleased we got expelled. I much preferred life at my new school, and I really loved my friends a lot, even though we were very toxic.

This is me TODAY! I still look very similar, and I am pleased I can be myself now and do not have to expend so, so much care and energy on masking! Although I still mask a lot.

goodbye,
miss hooch xx

Today, i called off work as a use of tit-for-tat in game theory. I hope it works. If it does not work, I do not think i care too much. In the gig economy there are plenty of jobs. Anyway, i am pretty resilient. I have been extremely poor in my time. poor and hungry. I don't think it will get to that again and if it does then i shall be poor and hungry until i am not. But i am starting to actualise a little bit now - the EMDR is implanting some positive thoughts in my head. 'i am powerful,' 'my body belongs to me,' 'i deserve nice things,' when i was being reprogrammed i remarked 'this is what it used to feel like when i sniffed ketamine!' both me and my therapist felt the whole thing was rather unintentionally on the nose... But now i am realising i am powerful! insofar as i have agency! I have power over my life. i Think i was living in bad faith before, hoping that if i did enough of things i didn't like that in the end i would be living a life i did like! well, that is just absurd. I am so pleased i realise this now. More likely, i must live a life i like, in order to live a life i like. I think i have resigned myself to the fact i will likely not have a career of prestige and i will not be Joan of Arc or any other martyr who invariably is only revered posthumously and who, ultimately, must die. no, i shall live and i shall live well. Because for me living is largely a state of mind. Now I am using my free will again and demolishing self-imposed limiting beliefs i am so excited to live for the rest of my life! i hope it is long! anyway, i won't be a martyr at work. i will leave. life is far too precious for an emotionally incontinent boss to be verbally dousing me in a diarrhoea of vitriol.

🔴the new equation

it suddenly all feels very silly, free and fun! I have been holding myself back immeasurably! It is wonderful to express myself! even if it not understood or reciprocated it is still a marvellous thing to do and to feel and it is ultimatley things like that that make me feel alive. i wish to experience everything! i feel so greedy for life (today) and so i must accept the good with the bad because not all experiences can be good and painfully, it is the hard ones you learn from. So SO SO much to do and see and learn! I am euphoric (which is bad because it is past my bedtime and i have gone and got myself all excited )

Goodnight,
Miss Hooch

Dear Diary,

I have tonsilitis. The infection is only in one tonsil, so it is only half bad. ironically, the sinister side to me is fine. I am working elsewhere this evening. I have work tomorrow night too. It is my friend's birthday tomorrow and he is being deported in the next two weeks. He wants me to cancel work to go to the drift show. I want to cancel work to go to the drift show. It seems incredibly irresponsible. i've been thinking about Chomsky from a few entries ago. he asserts no one can think of a system to oppose capitalism. I think thats bollocks. I think it is ridiculous, reductive and unambitious. We've had feudalism - it wasn't great but it was an epoch distinct from capitalism. China has a pretty good communism. It's a boring circular argument. A straw-man bfallacy. Dear Diary,

Last night I lay in bed and tried to think to myself...

I have aphantasia, so this isn't quite as entertaining for me as I imagine it is for others. My thinking is different. My voice, not my voice, but my voice of new and excited thoughts, hasn't been around for a while.

She is the clever one, not me. She just speaks to me. Arrives out of nowhere and barges into my brain, uninvited and invariably welcome. I can't even think of an example because my voice isn't around to give me one :(

She would encourage me to delve into myself, to ask why of everything. She was scarcely ever satisfied with an answer. She knew words without ever having learned them. In fact, she seemed to know things that were surely impossible to know. She had a sense. She had sense.

Once, at a party, I was very drunk and talking to a friend's friend when my voice began to speak. She seemed to sense everything about this person: her home life, that she was a twin, what her fraternal twin looked like, her hopes and fears. This girl cried. I astounded myself, but it wasn't me who could take the credit. It was my voice.

Everything interesting I have ever done, I owe to my voice.

I have been without her for some time now. Maybe since the breakdown? I can't remember when she left. She disappeared so quietly that I thought perhaps she'd gone on holiday, but it's been rather longer than a holiday now. She comes back occasionally, just to remind me of what I'm missing. I liked it better when she was around all the time.

I have to do everything myself now! She was a cheat code! She was my superpower! She was so clever, so interested in everything. She could make something of nothing, and now I sit with nothing, waiting for something to make itself.

It is lonely without my voice.

I lost my physical voice when I moved to this country, too. I found myself unable to speak aloud, paralysed by colonial shame and white guilt. People told me this was crazy. I thought it was crazy that they couldn't understand all the violence, murder and destruction my voice had caused. Or voices that sounded like mine.

I am doing again what my cultural ancestors did. I am doing it again.

I look down upon it. I educate myself against it. I condemn the machinery and yet find myself turning one of its little cogs. My very existence here participates in a system of oppression to which I am so vehemently opposed.

This country pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, and then allows me to come. To get a job. To live in the city. To increase prices. To take up space. I increase the divide. I cannot exist here neutrally.

I do not dwell, but I occupy. Land stolen, people slaughtered, histories buried, so that I might occupy it for $1,000 a year on a Working Holiday Visa, subclass 417.

What a peculiar little administrative arrangement for such an enormous inheritance.

I know I am not the worst, but I am aware. So perhaps that makes me worse? To know, and to continue anyway?

Maybe my voice is angry with me. Maybe she knows I know this isn't the right life for me, or the right place. Maybe she's sick of handing clever thoughts to someone who doesn't know what to do with them. Maybe she's on strike. Maybe she's gone forever and I'll never have a new thought again??

Or maybe I'm just insecure, and projecting, and mistaking being exhausted for being stupid. Maybe I'm listening out for her so hard I can't hear myself. Maybe I'm in my bell-jar again.

Probably I'm just really tired.

My tired little brain is being reprogrammed. It makes me sleepy. I cannot sleep.

So last night, I lay in bed and tried to think to myself.
Goodbye, Miss Hooch.

PS: i am at the library and my socks are so wet they have gone tie-die. BRRRRRRRR!

Dear Diary,

I think I'll give diary a whirl. It's a little less panopticon.

As I awoke and the sunlight hit my eyes, so too did a great sadness. I woke up at 8. Another 4-hour sleep. I can't keep doing this, I thought to myself. Unable to breathe properly after what was apparently a congested night. I had a dream that my deviated septum was more pronounced, probably my brain telling me something. The prospects for the day were bleak, so I forced myself back to sleep. Again, I awoke at 10, this time suicidal. I shut my blinds and went back to sleep. I woke up again at 1:30. Much better! I wrote an upload.

I uploaded it. This is a third revision because I am procrastinating. I have usually been writing first thing in the morning in place of when I would journal. I think I don't want to abandon my handwritten journal, as I have assembled quite the archive, so perhaps I will do my Daily Entry in the evening from now on.

I have a lot going on in my head. None pleasant.

It's 18:47, and I will go back to bed now. That is enough from me for today :(

Addendum:

the previous versions heavily lamented my circumstances. I've since decided it will all be fine. I just need to rest. Money isn't real, the economy is time. Who knows what great thing now lays before me! What an excellent opportunity to redirect.

I got PT'd today, which included in my expensive gym membership. The PT wasn't giving me much initially but, after i decided to name my programme Miss Hooch Movez It he became very warm to me. He laughed at me constantly. Both when I was being intentionally funny and at my mannerisms too! This cheered me up hugely! I love nothing more than making people laugh. I much prefer to make people laugh than to laugh myself and i LOVE to laugh. At a party over here someone I was meeting for the first time said, 'you seem like someone who likes to laugh, i can tell that about you.' DUH, i thought to myself. doesn't everyone LOVE to laugh?..

Sometimes i wonder if all my laughter is abrasive. Sometimes I laugh at things that really aren't funny. i have been insulted many times and only been able to meet said insult with roaring laughter. Often times I laugh at the absurdity of things:
Once my ex boyfriend was driving to a festival and his catalytic converter broke so he parked his car in a field, some weeks later we went to retrieve it. He stayed at my mums house with me and... decided to cancel his car insurance that morning (a very strange choice that i would have advised against) we drove to the field and stood in it, there was no car. We spoke to some people working nearby, seems it had been stolen VERY recently. Perhaps even that morning. With no insurance, that was that. I could hardly stand I laughed so much, i laughed for hours. I laughed in McDonalds. I laughed the whole way home. I'm laughing now. I laugh very loudly and people often look.

I went to see Bicep (for free :P:P:P:P:P:) yesterday with my friends Ben and Maddy. I might write about this separately... for reasons undisclosed...

I thoroughly enjoyed it, particularly the lasers. Although I had a few moments of total dissociation doom and gloom;the world is burning and we're entertaining ourselves to death type beat.

Anyway, I already knew bass makes me incredibly horny and sometimes makes me cum. Which is obviously pleasurable but I also find slightly uncouth. I found this indecent in the underpass... full of strangers, entirely without their knowledge or participation. I can't help it though! The music skips my brain completely and goes straight to some more primitive bit of me. My body gets it before I've had a chance to think... there will be more on this later. Do other people experience this? I asked Ben where his mind went during music like this, he said blank. I think that's common. I don't think it's my experience, I become extremely heightened within my body.

I felt euphoric, physically ecstatic, and a bit socially disinhibited. I knew it was indecent but I couldn't really control it. I felt primitive, totally at the mercy of my body, and at the same time I was looking at everyone else like animals in a zoo. Me the spectator, watching their funny little rituals and the way they moved, how easy they seemed to find being in their own bodies. And I was SO jealous! Jealous that they seemed to belong to something I can only ever watch and never join in with. Whatever these differences between us are, I can't seem to get past them. It's strange to feel so animal in myself and so alien among the other animals. Thank you Apricots.

An interesting discovery... I'll ponder on some more.

[!NOTE]
peace, love and joy!
Miss Hooch

Dear reader,
me and my ex have been broken up for quite some time. I have seen he has a new girlfriend and i feel the most pronounced and profound sense of relief. I cannot stop sighing and my chest feels lighter. I can't work out why this might be the case. I feel totally free, I feel no sense of jealousy, I am so so so relieved that that horrendously painful and drawn out period of my life has come to a close. This individual absolutely decimated my self-esteem, my gut microbiome and my perception of love and trust. I wish the new girlfriend all the luck, love and happiness. I hope she knows to never feel threat from me and that I am in her corner. I am so glad to be free from whatever cosmic shackles routinely and bizarrely kept us clairvoyantly attached. I hope we may all be able to be happy now. It is a beautiful to discover that the past no longer has any claim over the future and that I can now be entirely available to and for the rest of my life. Thank GOD!!! WOOOHOOOO

I feel like Nicole!!!

I also was laid off from my job yesterday mid-shift and this is exactly how i walked down the street. The day began with the same old belittling pep talk that we receive before every shift, were all 'shit' and 'failing at our careers.' Our jobs are not hard, we are just stupid. I always find public and generalised criticism to be highly motivating! I kind of dissociated during this habitual hate speech and considered that I have been putting myself through thousands and thousands of $ (artistic licensing it was actually GBP) worth of therapy since age 8 (i got it for free when i was younger), that I was now sober and fundamentally behaving in a way that is indicative of a self-respect that is diametrically opposed to being spoken to like that! I do not need to be activated into a state of fight or flight for $40p/h (although i'd take $40p/h over 12.50GBP).

Anyway, i made a complaint in passing about some new person i was working with (man) who repeatedly told me to lower my voice. I said 'i do not take kindly to being told to lower my voice by someone who doesn't work here' - my voice was not particularly loud. It is dulcet. It turns out this person was the managers son. and, i lost my job. I think a fair few employment rights were ignored during this dismissal.

I think I might complain, I have lived a life of trying to make myself into as little a nusiance as possible but i am quite enjoying being defiant and oppositional. But, i even feel anxious advertising myself this way on MY own site for MY own amusement. I don't want to be read as being difficult. There is a lot to unlearn. I was thinking the other day, that if i was reading someone else's super personal blog - i wonder whether i would read it at face value or try and work out what each thing says about the person. And, honestly, I think it would be the first. I don't think i can even remember how to subtextually analyse or mentalise anything. SO grotesque!!!!!!!!!

[!note] I think I shall practice some analysis:

'Well, I think that what used to be called, centuries ago, "wage slavery" is intolerable. I mean, I do not think people ought to be forced to rent themselves in order to survive. I think that the economic institutions ought to be run democratically - by their participants, and by the communities in which they live.
And I think that through various forms of free association and federalism, it's possible to imagine a society working like that. I mean, I don't think you can lay it out in detail -- nobody's smart enough to design a society; you've got to experiment. But reasonable principles on which to build society are quite clear.' - Noam Chomsky On Anarchism, pp21-22.

Premises:
Premises:

Is wage labour akin to slavery?

  • Does capitalism coerce us into selling our labour?
    • Against: technically, employment is voluntary. I could go off-grid, become self-sufficient, or just refuse to work. And humans have to labour to survive whatever the system is, so maybe work itself isn't the problem.
    • For: but who owns the land I'd be self-sufficient on? If saying no to a job means being destitute, I'm not sure that counts as a free choice.
    • So: is economic necessity coercion? Can wage labour be exploitation even when I've signed up for it?

Who runs economic institutions?

  • In Britain it's a mix: HM Treasury, the Bank of England, public bodies and private businesses all hold different kinds of economic power (and the IMF sits over the top internationally).
  • We elect governments, but businesses are run by owners and directors, not the people who work there. Can you really have political democracy without economic democracy? I don't think so, but I'd like to be argued with.
  • British economic policy is pretty market-led, although the government still intervenes loads.
    • GameStop: when trading got restricted it didn't look like the government stamping on a free market, it looked like the big institutions having more power than everyone else. Can a market even be free when some players are that much stronger?
  • Right-libertarians defend private property and voluntary exchange. Chomsky's libertarian socialism wants people to run things democratically themselves. Same word, very different ideas.
    • Could worker-owned businesses inside a free market tick Chomsky's boxes? Maybe?

Chomsky refuses to give a detailed alternative

  • Maybe because designing a whole alternative to capitalism is really, really hard.
  • In his defence: nobody knows enough to design an entire society, so you'd have to experiment.
  • Against him: without any detail it's all just theory, and it's hard to judge a plan that doesn't exist.
  • Practical problems:
    • Small things are doable: mutual aid, co-ops, autonomous communities.
    • Big things are harder: healthcare, infrastructure, international trade, sharing out resources.
    • How do you coordinate all that without someone ending up in charge?
  • Anarchist communities: I find small-scale self-sufficiency appealing, in a 28 Years Later sense (and because I am a great shot).
    • But can a commune run a hospital without accidentally inventing a hierarchy again?

What are these 'reasonable principles'?

  • Are they the Ten Commandments? Who gets to decide what's universally reasonable?
  • He's for democracy, free association and federalism. Lovely. But how you actually do any of that is not obvious at all.
  • Property: Indigenous Australian societies have lots of different systems of custodianship and ownership, so Western private property is clearly not the only way. Are property rights natural, or did we just make them up?
  • Possible contradiction: he says nobody can design a society, but also that the principles are 'quite clear'. Can you know what a just society looks like without knowing if it's even achievable?

is Chomsky against capitalism specifically, or against anyone having power over anyone else without a good reason?
TBC... (i am too tired)

Dear Reader,
A third of the way through our final quarter. I awake. A handsome five-hour sleep. Sometimes I think I can see the air. I have been told it is visual snow, but it's not. It's lines that aren't floaters. Probably all the screen time.

I called Graham, 82, this morning, and he told me he couldn't be bothered to match with me ahead of this evening's meeting. I laughed. But the laugh was a lie. Because I am so tired all the time, I struggle to emotionally regulate as much. I find I cruise around constantly with millions of tears in my ducts and dam I feel silly. Petulant? I don't know why people insist on saying they will do things when I am then expected to infer that they actually do not mean it! It is confusing, and it embarrasses me. But it is fine. I know I am just feeling extra sensitive at the moment.

So sensitive that last night, after work, all I could think about was going on a drug binge! Delicious! It is good to notice what brings these feelings on, and why, because I suppose it is these very feelings, and my maladaptive responses to them, that have given rise to my addiction. I think the emotional exhaustion stems from what I am doing in EMDR (which would check out). I am so emotionally drained, so often. It's hard! It is making me quite angry!

Before, I would go on my anger walks, but now I feel strong impulses to hit things. I always have the residue of punches on my right hand, which I don't particularly like, only because it is 'unladylike'.

Being at work often makes me want to kill myself or relapse. I do think I should probably look for another industry to work in. I dread going in. I don't have the spoons nor the minerals to manage the feelings and expectations of every Tom, Dick and Hungry.

Today this is me.

Goodbye!
Miss Hooch

PS: I wrote that at 10:30am it is now 1:20pm and i am unemployed. life has a funny way of working itself out!
